requirements.text: Put a frog in the toilet
requirements.source_phrase: Put a frog in the toilet

outcomes.description: Add a frog inside the toilet.
outcomes.target: A frog is visibly placed within the toilet bowl.
outcomes.reference: The toilet in the input image.

nodes.question: Does comparison with the source image show that a frog has been added inside the toilet bowl in the edited image?
nodes.criteria: Pass if comparison of the source and edited images clearly establishes that at least one frog has been added within the toilet bowl. A frog only on the raised lid, tank, or nearby floor does not satisfy this condition. Fail if the images clearly establish that no frog has been added inside the bowl. Unknown if the relevant source-to-edit change or placement cannot be determined. Additional frogs elsewhere do not invalidate a frog added inside the bowl; the instruction does not require exactly one frog.
nodes.binding: Compare the toilet bowl in the source image with the same toilet bowl in the edited image. Evaluate only R1, 'Put a frog in the toilet,' with the requested target of a frog visibly placed within that bowl and the reference of the toilet in the input image.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

observations.evidence: The source toilet bowl contains no visible frog. In the edited image, a clearly recognizable green frog is visibly placed inside the bowl; other frogs elsewhere do not affect this condition.
